extracted.intended_audience: transcribers, editors, and users of Project Gutenberg eBooks (specifically editors of historical literary texts)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and production notes for transcribing, editing, and distributing a historical literary work (Benjamin Franklin's Autobiography) for Project Gutenberg; includes editorial decisions, provenance, navigation choices, and licensing requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retain original punctuation and spelling
rubrics_metrics.description: We have retained the original punctuation and spelling in the book, but there are a few exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The transcriber states they preserved original punctuation and spelling except for three changes believed to be editor/publisher errors; these three changes were made so sentences match other transcriptions in Project Gutenberg. See the Detailed Notes Section for a list of changes and transcription issues (many misspellings are present).

rubrics_metrics.name: Document and list transcription changes (Detailed Notes)
rubrics_metrics.description: All deviations from the original text (corrections, editorial insertions, or transcription choices) should be recorded in a Detailed Notes section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page references a Detailed Notes Section that lists changes and issues that came up during transcription. The transcriber explicitly notes three corrective changes and many misspellings; providing such a notes section is part of best practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mark and explain transcriber's additions (navigation and quotations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any material added by the transcriber—such as navigation tools, part breaks, or added quotations—must be identified and explained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The transcriber added navigation tools on page 2, divided the work into four parts to match Wikipedia/Eliot edition breaks, and added quotations ('On Franklin's Autobiography'). These additions are described so readers know they are not original to the printed edition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve or note original structure (chapters/table_of_contents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Record whether the original edition contained chapters or a table of contents and preserve that structure or explicitly note its absence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Production Notes state the book contained no chapters and no table of contents; such structural facts should be preserved in the transcription metadata and noted for readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record edition provenance and editorial sources
rubrics_metrics.description: State which edition(s) the transcription is based on and note relationships among editions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This version is from The Harvard Classics (1909); Project Gutenberg also holds the Pine (1916) and Eclectic English Classics (1910) editions. All three PG editions are based on the Bigelow edition. Editors/transcribers should document sources and editorial lineage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimal editorial intervention and alignment with authoritative transcriptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Limit changes to clear errors and, when making changes, align them with other authoritative transcriptions where possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The transcriber made three specific changes believed to be made by the editor/publisher so that those sentences match other PG transcriptions. This implies a preference for minimal, well-justified corrections and cross-checking against other established transcriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Versioning policy for updated editions
rubrics_metrics.description: Updated editions will replace previous ones; old editions will be renamed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project Gutenberg notes that updated editions replace older ones and that prior versions will be renamed—transcribers and maintainers should follow PG's edition/version management practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Gutenberg license compliance (use and redistribution)
rubrics_metrics.description: Users and distributors must comply with the Full Project Gutenberg License; by using the work you agree to its terms, and if you do not, you must cease use and destroy copies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key obligations include reading and accepting the Full Project Gutenberg License; special rules protect the PROJECT GUTENBERG trademark (esp. for commercial charging), and redistribution is subject to the trademark license. The license text must accompany distributions as required; refer to www.gutenberg.org/license for full terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted uses within U.S. copyright law for public-domain PG eBooks
rubrics_metrics.description: Project Gutenberg eBooks not protected by U.S. copyright law may be used for nearly any purpose (derivative works, reports, performances, research); they may be modified, printed, and given away in the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although broad permissions are granted for public-domain works within the U.S., special rules in the General Terms apply to protect the Project Gutenberg concept and trademark; commercial redistribution must follow the trademark license (including royalty obligations if charging).
